description: Versioned SharePoint capture (integrations/capture_sharepoint.py) through the GET-only Graph client: walks the configured scope (QCQA '/AOs/2026 - AOs' by drive id, the AGENTS site's '/Ontology UseCases' resolved by site name), reads every listed item's permissions, downloads each new version's bytes (bounded, sha256-pinned) and extracts its text (a PDF page by page; scanned pages OCR-read locally by poppler + tesseract, never a network service), all kept in the check's temporary Workbench state (outside the git tree). Run 1 captures, run 2 re-walks and must keep every unchanged version (no new versions without an eTag change). Then the store is read back offline: every captured handle resolves, every captured content re-hashes, an actor without a grant sees 0 roots, 0 rows, 0 counts, and a folder-only actor (the captured folders granted, item permissions required, no source identity: the shape of an employee whose folder grant is wider than the files shared with them) sees 0 rows, 0 counts and resolves nothing. Counts, booleans and enums only; no names, paths, ids, permissions or content.
notes: Live-unverified until the live check runs it (evidence label of the injected-transport tests: integrations/tests/test_capture_sharepoint.py, ontology/tests/test_sharepoint_documents.py). Captured files live in the named host state sharepoint-capture-check-live-check under $PLX_WORKBENCH_STATE_DIR (--state-name live-check), kept between runs and never shared with the default store; nothing captured is printed. A root is complete when every listed item has a terminal outcome: its bytes captured, or a file over the content cap (20 MB) recorded as such with its metadata, size, permissions and version kept and its content skipped. Such files are counted apart in summary.content_exceeds_cap (recorded, never hidden, never a reason to raise the cap) and per run in counts.contents_exceeds_cap. A root that stops incomplete fails the check with its reason: listing_truncated, withheld_from_capture, depth_bound, folder_bound, not_visible, source_error:<detail>, or content_incomplete (a file whose bytes could not be read; it is still a captured version, never absent, and summary.content_unavailable > 0 fails the check visibly). Unverified live assumptions: the AGENTS site resolves on the SHAREPOINT_SITE_ID host; the shared app may read item permissions; the runner host has poppler and tesseract (the scanned AOs have no text layer; without them summary.texts_ocr_unavailable > 0 fails the check visibly) and the scans OCR to text. Scope: examples/sharepoint_capture_scope.live-check.json (the two folders this check was written for; passes took 250-310 s). Live 2026-10-05 on ff2879cb timed out at 1800 s: the check still named integrations/sharepoint_capture_scope.json after it was widened to the whole QA/QC library and PLXCUSTOMERS Customer Documents (max_folders 5000 each), a serial walk that downloads, hashes and OCR-reads every new file. --budget-seconds 1500 bounds the capture's wall time below the timeout: a root it cuts is incomplete with reason time_budget (never reconciled, never complete), so a slow source fails with a reported partial state, never a timeout. registry_names: the source registry credits a Graph endpoint template only through operations_read, the grammar operations (integrations/live_source_grammar.py) this run's GETs were answered for; an endpoint no operation folds to is never credited by this check. Mirror regress (daily 2026-10-21T01:25:50Z: summary.roots_complete 1 of 2, the 1301-file ~969 MB QCQA AOs root incomplete in both runs at --budget-seconds 1500 over a fresh {tmp}/state, before the store was kept as described above; storage.carried is true from the second day): a root the budget cuts resumes from its stored walk position in the next daily run and the check passes once every root has completed; until then it fails, never passes on a partial root, and incomplete_scope names each incomplete root (target id, root ordinal, typed reasons, resumable, persisted, later_ask live-host-persistent-state-dir where the store is not kept). Live-unverified until two daily runs show roots_complete rising. Blocked, never passed: when every root left incomplete is cut by the time budget alone and its store is not kept between runs, the report's blocked_upstream names each (cause later_ask, live-host-persistent-state-dir) and expect_blocked checks the rest (no leak, no unavailable content, files captured; the re-walk's new versions are not asserted, run 2 continues the cut walk). A cut root over a kept store (--state-name, workbench_state_dir) resumes next run and fails meanwhile; any other incomplete reason fails.
